mainTopic: The shape of the לחם הפנים (open box or rocking boat), and how each shape works with the bowls, rods and side panels on the שולחן.
overview: רבי חנינא and רבי יוחנן disagree about the shape of the לחם הפנים. רבי חנינא says it was like an open box: a flat, wide bottom with straight walls. רבי יוחנן says it was like a rocking boat: a narrow bottom with walls slanting outward. The גמרא first raises three challenges against the boat shape, about the בזיכין (frankincense bowls), the קנים (rods between the loaves) and the סניפין (side panels). Each one is answered with a small practical adjustment. Then the גמרא turns to the open-box view. It explains that there the סניפין carry the weight so the lower loaves don't break. It also explains that in that view the סניפין stood on the ground, as רבי אבא בר ממל says. Finally, רבי יהודה's statement that the loaves and panels hold each other up is shown to fit only the rocking-boat view.

steps.title: Two views on the shape of the shewbread
steps.stepSummary: רבי חנינא says the לחם הפנים looked like an open box. רבי יוחנן says it looked like a rocking boat.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי חנינא says: like an open box. רבי יוחנן says: like a rocking boat.
steps.whatsHappening: Two אמוראים give different descriptions of what the לחם הפנים looked like.
steps.deeperAnalysis: An 'open box' means a flat, wide bottom with two straight walls going up, open on two sides. A 'rocking boat' means a narrow bottom with walls slanting outward, so it would tip from side to side. The rest of the passage tests how each shape would work on the שולחן.

keyTerms.meaning: The shewbread, the twelve loaves placed on the שולחן in the מקדש
An open box, flat-bottomed and open on two sides
A rocking boat, with a narrow bottom and slanted sides

steps.whyThisMatters: Each of the three questions that follow depends on this disagreement about shape.

phrases.english: Rabbi Chanina says:
Like an open box.
Rabbi Yochanan says:
Like a rocking boat.
phrases.notes: Picture a V-shaped boat. Its narrow bottom makes it rock back and forth.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי חֲנִינָא אָמַר: כְּמִין תֵּיבָה פְּרוּצָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens the passage with a disagreement about the loaf's shape.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי חנינא: the loaf is box-shaped. רבי יוחנן: the loaf is boat-shaped.

steps.title: How could the frankincense bowls rest on a boat-shaped loaf?
steps.stepSummary: With a box shape, the בזיכין sit easily on the flat top. With a boat shape, where would they rest?
steps.simpleTranslation: It makes sense for the one who says 'like an open box': that is how the bowls could rest. But for the one who says 'like a rocking boat', how could the bowls rest?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רבי יוחנן. A loaf with slanted sides seems to have no flat spot for the frankincense bowls.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The בזיכין of frankincense had to be placed with the לחם הפנים. A box-shaped loaf has a flat area that can hold them. A loaf with a narrow, slanted shape seems to leave nowhere stable to put them.

keyTerms.meaning: Granted, this works fine (opens a comparison that leads into a challenge)
The bowls of frankincense placed with the לחם הפנים

steps.confusionAlert: 'בשלמא... אלא' does not mean the גמרא is ruling for רבי חנינא. It is a standard challenge pattern: one view fits easily, so how does the other view explain the same thing?

phrases.english: Granted, according to the one who says
like an open box,
that is how the bowls could rest there.
But according to the one who says
like a rocking boat,
how could the bowls rest there?

steps.triggerLanguage: בִּשְׁלָמָא לְמַאן דְּאָמַר כְּמִין תֵּיבָה פְּרוּצָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Tests רבי יוחנן's shape against a practical need.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A boat shape has no flat surface for the בזיכין to sit on.

steps.title: A flat spot was made for the bowls
steps.stepSummary: The baker formed a flat place on the loaf where the בזיכין could sit.
steps.simpleTranslation: He made a place for them.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers: when the loaf was made, a flat spot was shaped into it so the bowls could rest there.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The loaf was still boat-shaped overall. It just had a small flat area added. The answer keeps רבי יוחנן's view and explains how it would work in practice.

keyTerms.meaning: A place, here a flat spot

phrases.english: He made a place for them.
phrases.notes: 'He' means whoever shaped the loaf. 'Them' means the bowls.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge about the bowls.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: A boat-shaped loaf cannot hold the bowls.
steps.terutzMaskana: A flat spot was shaped into the loaf for the bowls.

steps.title: How could the rods rest on a boat-shaped loaf?
steps.stepSummary: The loaves were stacked with קנים between them. A wide, flat loaf can rest on several rods, but a narrow-bottomed loaf seems unable to.
steps.simpleTranslation: It makes sense for the one who says 'like an open box': that is how the rods could rest. But for the one who says 'like a rocking boat', how could the rods rest?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a second challenge to רבי יוחנן, this time about the rods between the stacked loaves.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The loaves were stacked on the שולחן with קנים between them so air could pass through. A flat-bottomed loaf sits steadily across several rods. A V-shaped loaf touches only one rod at the bottom and would tip over.

keyTerms.meaning: The rods placed between the stacked loaves
The golden table in the מקדש where the loaves were arranged

phrases.english: Granted, according to the one who says
like an open box,
that is how the rods could rest.
But according to the one who says
like a rocking boat,
how could the rods rest?

steps.triggerLanguage: בִּשְׁלָמָא לְמַאן דְּאָמַר כְּמִין תֵּיבָה פְּרוּצָה – הַיְינוּ דַּהֲווֹ יָתְבִי קָנִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second challenge using the same pattern as step 2.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A narrow-bottomed loaf cannot rest steadily on the rods.

steps.title: A small base was added to the loaf
steps.stepSummary: The baker made a bump at the bottom of the loaf so it could rest on the rods.
steps.simpleTranslation: He made a protrusion for them.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that a small extension was formed at the narrow bottom of the loaf, making it wide enough to sit on the rods.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The answer follows the same idea as step 3. The basic boat shape stays, and a small change makes it practical. The widened base lets the loaf rest on more than one rod.

keyTerms.meaning: A protrusion or bump, here a small widened base

phrases.english: He made a protrusion for them.
phrases.notes: A little bump at the narrow bottom of the loaf, so it sits steadily on the rods.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge about the rods.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: A V-shaped loaf would tip over on the rods.
steps.terutzMaskana: A small base was added so the loaf rests steadily.

steps.title: How could the side panels support a boat-shaped loaf?
steps.stepSummary: Upright סניפין held the loaves in place. They fit straight walls well, but slanted walls would touch them only at the top edge.
steps.simpleTranslation: It makes sense for the one who says 'like an open box': that is how the panels support the bread. But for the one who says 'like a rocking boat', how could the panels support the bread?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a third challenge to רבי יוחנן, about the side panels that held the loaves in place.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The סניפין stood straight up at the sides of the שולחן and braced the loaves. Straight-walled loaves press flat against them. Slanted walls would touch the panels only at their upper edges and give weak support.

keyTerms.meaning: Upright panels at the sides of the שולחן that held the loaves in place

phrases.english: Granted, according to the one who says
like an open box,
that is how the panels support the bread.
But according to the one who says
like a rocking boat,
how could the panels support the bread?

steps.triggerLanguage: בִּשְׁלָמָא לְמַאן דְּאָמַר כְּמִין תֵּיבָה פְּרוּצָה – הַיְינוּ דְּסָמְכִי לֵיהּ סְנִיפִין לְלֶחֶם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A third challenge using the same pattern.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Straight upright panels cannot press properly against slanted walls.

steps.title: The panels were bent to match the loaf
steps.stepSummary: The סניפין were made curved or angled to fit the slanted sides of the loaf.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the panels were bent inward to match the slanted shape of the loaf, so they supported it along its whole side.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This time the change is to the panels, not to the bread. With this third answer, all three challenges to רבי יוחנן are resolved and his view still stands. Next, the גמרא turns around and challenges רבי חנינא's open-box view.

keyTerms.meaning: Made curved or rounded, here bent at an angle

steps.whatToRemember: רבי יוחנן's rocking-boat view survives all three challenges. Every practical question about the boat shape (bowls, rods, panels) is answered with a small adjustment.

phrases.english: That they were made curved.
phrases.notes: 'They' here are the panels, bent to match the slanted sides of the loaf.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge about the panels.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Adjusting the panels to the shape
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Straight panels cannot support slanted loaves.
steps.terutzMaskana: The panels were bent to fit the loaves.

steps.title: Why would the open-box view need panels at all?
steps.stepSummary: The rocking-boat view clearly needs סניפין, but the open-box view seems not to need them.
steps.simpleTranslation: Granted, according to the one who said the loaves were like a rocking boat, that is why we need panels. But according to the one who said they were like an open box, why do I need panels?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the open-box opinion: if the loaves have a wide, flat bottom, why would they need סניפין to hold them up?
steps.deeperAnalysis: A loaf shaped like a rocking boat has a narrow bottom and slanted sides, so it cannot stand alone and needs support. A loaf shaped like an open box stands firmly on its own wide base. So the סניפין seem to have no job in that view.

keyTerms.meaning: Why do I need it? What is it for?

steps.confusionAlert: Both opinions agree that there were סניפין. The question is not whether they existed, but what job they had in the open-box view.

phrases.english: Granted, according to the one who said
like a kind of rocking boat
this is why we need panels,
phrases.notes: A boat-shaped loaf can't stand alone on its narrow bottom, so it needs something holding it.

phrases.english: but according to the one who said
like a kind of open box
why do I need panels?

steps.triggerLanguage: בִּשְׁלָמָא לְמַאן דְּאָמַר כְּמִין סְפִינָה רוֹקֶדֶת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Having explained how the סניפין fit the slanted loaf, the גמרא now asks whether the other opinion needs סניפין at all.
steps.kashyaTarget: The open-box view of the loaf's shape
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A loaf with a wide, flat base stands by itself, so support panels seem pointless.

steps.title: The panels keep the lower loaves from breaking
steps.stepSummary: Without the panels, the weight of the upper loaves would crush the lower ones.
steps.simpleTranslation: Because of the weight of the bread, the lower loaves would break.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that even box-shaped loaves need סניפין, because otherwise the loaves would be stacked straight on top of each other and the bottom ones would crack.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the open-box view, the סניפין are not there to keep the loaves from falling over. Their job is to carry the weight, so each loaf does not press down on the one beneath it. This gives the סניפין a real purpose in that view too.

phrases.english: due to the weight of the bread, it would break.
phrases.notes: He means the upper loaves pressing down would crack the lower ones.

steps.terutzResolutionType: Gives the panels a different purpose in the open-box view
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Panels exist only to keep unstable loaves from falling.
steps.terutzMaskana: In the open-box view, panels carry weight and protect the lower loaves from being crushed.

steps.title: Where would the panels stand in the open-box view?
steps.stepSummary: In the open-box view the loaves fill the table, so there seems to be no room on it for the panels.
steps.simpleTranslation: Granted, according to the one who said they were like a rocking boat, the panels rest on the table. But according to the one who said they were like an open box, where would he put the panels? Would he put them on the ground?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא raises a new difficulty for the open-box view: where could the סניפין be placed?
steps.deeperAnalysis: A boat-shaped loaf is narrow at the bottom, so there is space on the שלחן beside it for the panels. A box-shaped loaf is wide at the bottom and takes up the whole width of the שלחן, leaving no room. Putting the panels on the floor sounds strange, so the גמרא asks it as a challenge.

phrases.english: Granted, according to the one who said
like a kind of rocking boat
the panels are placed on the table.
But according to the one who said
like a kind of open box
where does he place the panels?
phrases.notes: The wide bottom of a box-shaped loaf reaches the edges of the table, so there is no space left on it.

phrases.english: Does he place them on the ground?

steps.triggerLanguage: בִּשְׁלָמָא לְמַאן דְּאָמַר כְּמִין סְפִינָה רוֹקֶדֶת – סְנִיפִין עַל גַּבֵּי שֻׁלְחָן מוּנָּחִין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Accepts that the open-box view needs panels, then asks where they could physically stand.
steps.kashyaTarget: Where the סניפין are placed in the open-box view
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A wide-based loaf leaves no space on the שלחן, and placing panels on the floor seems unlikely.

steps.title: Yes, the panels stood on the ground
steps.stepSummary: רבי אבא בר ממל confirms that in the open-box view, the panels stood on the floor.
steps.simpleTranslation: Yes, as רבי אבא בר ממל said: according to the one who says they were like a rocking boat, the panels rest on the table; according to the one who says they were like an open box, the panels rest on the ground.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא accepts the strange-sounding idea and backs it up with a statement of רבי אבא בר ממל: in the open-box view, the סניפין really did stand on the floor.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The challenge assumed that panels on the ground made no sense, but the גמרא says that is exactly how it was. רבי אבא בר ממל spells out both views side by side: on the table for the boat shape, on the ground for the box shape. So the open-box view stays intact.

keyTerms.meaning: According to the words of the one who says

steps.whatToRemember: Rocking boat: the panels stand on the שלחן and hold up unstable loaves. Open box: the panels stand on the ground and carry the weight so the lower loaves don't break.

phrases.aramaic: אִין, דְּאָמַר רַבִּי אַבָּא בַּר מֶמֶל:
phrases.english: Yes, as Rabbi Abba bar Memel said:
according to the one who says like a kind of rocking boat,
the panels are placed on the table;
according to the one who says like a kind of open box,
the panels are placed on the ground.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִין, דְּאָמַר רַבִּי אַבָּא בַּר מֶמֶל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 10 by accepting its suggestion and supporting it with an אמורא's statement.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Accepts the suggested option and supports it with a source
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Panels on the ground make no sense, so the open-box view has a problem.
steps.terutzMaskana: In the open-box view, the panels did stand on the ground, as רבי אבא בר ממל states.

steps.title: Which view fits רבי יהודה's statement?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks which opinion matches רבי יהודה's statement that the loaves and the panels hold each other up.
steps.simpleTranslation: Whose view does רבי יהודה's statement follow: 'The bread holds up the panels, and the panels hold up the bread'?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a statement of רבי יהודה and asks which of the two shape opinions it matches.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יהודה describes support going both ways: the loaves lean on the panels and the panels lean on the loaves. That only works if the panels and loaves actually rest against each other. The question sets up a test of which shape allows that.

phrases.english: In accordance with whom is this
that Rabbi Yehuda said:
the bread holds up the panels,
and the panels hold up the bread?

steps.triggerLanguage: כְּמַאן אָזְלָא הָא דְאָמַר רַבִּי יְהוּדָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After placing the panels in each view, the גמרא uses that picture to fit רבי יהודה's statement to one view.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which shape opinion matches רבי יהודה's description of loaves and panels supporting each other.

steps.title: It fits the rocking-boat view
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהודה's statement matches the view that the loaves were shaped like a rocking boat.
steps.simpleTranslation: It follows the one who said they were like a rocking boat.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that רבי יהודה's statement fits the rocking-boat view.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the rocking-boat view, the panels stand on the שלחן right next to the slanted loaves, so the two lean on each other. In the open-box view, the panels stand on the floor and hold themselves up, so they do not need the loaves to support them. The support goes only one way there, so רבי יהודה's two-way support fits only the boat shape.
steps.whatToRemember: The shape of the loaf decides where the סניפין stand and what job they do. רבי יהודה's two-way support only works in the rocking-boat view.

phrases.english: In accordance with the one who said like a kind of rocking boat.

steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: רבי יהודה's statement follows the rocking-boat view, where the panels on the שלחן and the slanted loaves lean on each other.
